To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the design of proton linear accelerators for energies up to 300 MeV requires minimization of the power losses by optimization of cavity and drift-tubes parameters.
the use of ellipsoidal drift tubes can significantly reduce the power losses of a linear accelerator, and that the power losses can be further reduced by using an elliptical shape for the cavity.
the power loss in proton linear accelerator drift tubes increases with the square of the drift-tube radius and the drift-tube length and is proportional to the square of the accelerating frequency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a proton linear accelerator for energies of about 300 Mev.
the design and development of proton linear accelerators for use at energies up to 300 Mev.
the design of a proton linear accelerator for energies up to 200 Mev, and with the design and development of the necessary components for such an accelerator.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the 2 pi structure, as presently designed and constructed, has a power loss of 1.5 to 1.7 kw/mw at 50 Mev, increasing linearly to about 3 kw/mw at an energy of 200 Mev, and is limited by power losses to a maximum energy of about 200 Mev.
the present design of the proton linear accelerator is a practical and economical one for energies of up to about 200 MeV and that the design can probably be extended to energies of up to 300 MeV.
the design of a linear proton accelerator for 300-Mev operation is possible, and the power loss per unit length can be reduced to 0.1 to 0.2 kw/meter, with the possibility of further reduction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the feasibility of the 2 pi structure at 200 Mev and have indicated a possible way of reducing power losses at high energy.
, in order to obtain a 300 Mev proton beam of 1 Mev energy spread, a 200 Mev linac with a 1.5 Mev beam energy spread is required.
a proton linear accelerator with an energy of 300 MeV is possible with a power of 100 MW.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of ellipsoidal drift tubes in a 200 MeV linear proton accelerator would reduce power losses due to surface currents by 20%.
we can now design and build a 300 MeV proton linear accelerator.
the design of proton linear accelerators for energies above 200 MeV can be optimized for power efficiency by using a cylindrical geometry with a specific set of dimensions, which we provide.
